_note: States with a bed bug disclosure or treatment statute. rule carries the citation inline.
_notice: General reference, not legal advice. Statutes change and vary by jurisdiction; verify every figure against the current official state code before relying on it. Last reviewed 2026-05.

AZ.rule: A.R.S. § 33-1319: requires landlord and tenant duties regarding bed bug treatment and disclosure

CA.rule: Cal. Civ. Code §§ 1954.600-1954.605 (eff. 2017): written notice to all new tenants and existing tenants; cannot rent unit with known infestation; notify within 2 business days of pest control findings

CT.rule: Conn. Gen. Stat. § 47a-7a: bedbug infestation disclosure and treatment standards

FL.rule: Fla. Stat. § 83.51(2) (general habitability): bedbugs covered; specific disclosure not required, but treatment obligation exists

MA.rule: 105 CMR 410.550 (sanitary code): treatment obligation; some municipalities (Boston Inspectional Services Dept.) require disclosure

ME.rule: 14 M.R.S. § 6021-A: landlord must disclose bedbug infestation in adjacent units; must respond to tenant report within 5 days

MI.rule: Mich. Comp. Laws § 333.12601 et seq. (Michigan Bed Bug Notification Act): pre-tenancy disclosure required

NJ.rule: N.J. Admin. Code § 5:10-2: multi-family dwellings must conduct annual inspections; disclose infestation history

NY.rule: NYC Admin. Code § 27-2018.1: annual bedbug infestation history disclosure required (NYC); DHCR form must accompany every vacancy lease

OH.rule: Ohio Rev. Code § 5321.04 (general); local: Cincinnati, Cleveland require disclosure

TX.rule: Tex. Prop. Code § 92.052 (general habitability): bedbugs covered under habitability obligation; no specific disclosure statute

VA.rule: Va. Code § 55.1-1223: disclose any known bedbug infestation in last 12 months

WA.rule: RCW 59.18.060 (general habitability): bedbugs covered; Seattle and Tacoma have specific disclosure ordinances
